item.title: Basic Verification of Custom CRD Design and Controller Implementation with Kubebuilder
item.description:
In the process of operating a Kubernetes cluster, relying solely on standard primitives such as Pods, Services, and Deployments introduces challenges where domain-specific lifecycle management and declarative state maintenance cannot be fully automated. Because ad-hoc operations using shell scripts or external scripts are prone to human error and state drift, it becomes necessary to apply the Operator pattern—registering custom resource types directly into the Kubernetes Control Plane and managing their lifecycle via the API server.

This article outlines the workflow from formulating a Custom Resource Definition (CRD) schema using the Kubebuilder framework to implementing a state-tracking controller via a Reconcile loop and verifying connectivity in a local environment.

1. Components of the Kubernetes Extension Architecture

The Kubernetes extension mechanism is based on a feedback control model that reconciles the declared specification (Desired State) with the actual system state (Actual State).

  • Custom Resource (CR): An instance of a user-defined custom object. Data is persisted to etcd, the cluster’s storage backend, enabling CRUD operations via the API server.
  • Custom Resource Definition (CRD): The blueprint defining the OpenAPI v3 schema of a CR. It specifies field type validation, required checks, and the presence or absence of status subresources.
  • Controller: An autonomous process that watches for events (create, update, delete) on specified resources and executes a Reconcile() function within an infinite loop structure to eliminate discrepancies.

Characteristics of Development Framework Options

For implementing Kubernetes controllers, Kubebuilder and Operator SDK are the two primary options. Their characteristics are compared below:

Item Kubebuilder Operator SDK
Primary Maintainer Kubernetes SIGs Operator Framework (CNCF/Red Hat)
Supported Languages Go Go, Ansible, Helm
Scope Scaffolding, code generation, testing Scaffolding, OLM integration, packaging
Structural Relationship Standard core for controller implementation Adopts Kubebuilder internally as the engine for Go-based implementations

In this implementation, Kubebuilder is adopted to minimize dependencies and rapidly verify pure Go controller logic.

2. Project Initialization and API Schema Definition

First, create a working directory and run scaffolding by specifying the project domain and repository module name.

mkdir cinema-operator && cd cinema-operator
kubebuilder init --domain cinema.com --repo cinema.com/operator

Next, generate the API resource structure with group name entertainment, version v1, and Kind name Movie.

kubebuilder create api --group entertainment --version v1 --kind Movie

Edit the generated api/v1/movie_types.go and declare domain-specific fields in MovieSpec.

package v1

import (
 metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
)

type MovieSpec struct {
 Title string `json:"title,omitempty"`
 Genre string `json:"genre,omitempty"`
 RunningTime int `json:"runningTime,omitempty"`
 IsReleased bool `json:"isReleased,omitempty"`
}

type MovieStatus struct {
 // Add status fields for state management as necessary
}

// +kubebuilder:object:root=true
// +kubebuilder:subresource:status

type Movie struct {
 metav1.TypeMeta `json:",inline"`
 metav1.ObjectMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`

 Spec MovieSpec `json:"spec,omitempty"`
 Status MovieStatus `json:"status,omitempty"`
}

// +kubebuilder:object:root=true

type MovieList struct {
 metav1.TypeMeta `json:",inline"`
 metav1.ListMeta `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
 Items []Movie `json:"items"`
}

func init() {
 SchemeBuilder.Register(&Movie{}, &MovieList{})
}

3. Implementing Controller Reconcile Logic

Implement the processing flow upon event detection in internal/controller/movie_controller.go. Retrieve the instance of the target resource from the API server; if it does not exist, ignore the NotFound error and terminate the loop.

package controller

import (
 "context"

 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime"
 ctrl "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/log"

 entertainmentv1 "cinema.com/operator/api/v1"
)

type MovieReconciler struct {
 client.Client
 Scheme *runtime.Scheme
}

// +kubebuilder:rbac:groups=entertainment.cinema.com,resources=movies,verbs=get;list;watch;create;update;patch;delete
// +kubebuilder:rbac:groups=entertainment.cinema.com,resources=movies/status,verbs=get;update;patch

func (r *MovieReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) (ctrl.Result, error) {
 logger := log.FromContext(ctx)

 var movie entertainmentv1.Movie
 if err := r.Get(ctx, req.NamespacedName, &movie); err != nil {
 return ctrl.Result{}, client.IgnoreNotFound(err)
 }

 logger.Info("Reconciling Movie resource", 
 "Name", movie.Name, 
 "Title", movie.Spec.Title, 
 "Genre", movie.Spec.Genre,
 "RunningTime", movie.Spec.RunningTime,
 "IsReleased", movie.Spec.IsReleased,
 )

 return ctrl.Result{}, nil
}

func (r *MovieReconciler) SetupWithManager(mgr ctrl.Manager) error {
 return ctrl.NewControllerManagedBy(mgr).
 For(&entertainmentv1.Movie{}).
 Complete(r)
}

4. Manifest Generation and Local Endpoint Verification

Automatically generate CRD manifest files from the marker comments (+kubebuilder:...) attached to the Go structs.

make manifests

Apply the generated manifest file config/crd/bases/entertainment.cinema.com_movies.yaml to the verification API server. Below is the procedure to launch a temporary container for development verification and register the resource.

docker run -d --name=k8s-api --net=host \
 registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.19.0 \
 kube-apiserver --etcd-servers=http://127.0.0.1:8888 \
 --authorization-mode=AlwaysAllow --bind-address=0.0.0.0 \
 --insecure-port=8080 --secure-port=6444 --allow-privileged=true

kubectl --server=http://127.0.0.1:8080 apply -f config/crd/bases/entertainment.cinema.com_movies.yaml

Write a CR instance manifest movie-sample.yaml that conforms to the defined schema.

apiVersion: entertainment.cinema.com/v1
kind: Movie
metadata:
 name: the-outlaws
spec:
 title: "The Outlaws 4"
 genre: "Action"
 runningTime: 109
 isReleased: true

Register the CR into the cluster.

kubectl --server=http://127.0.0.1:8080 apply -f movie-sample.yaml

Start the controller process and synchronize it with the API server.

export KUBERNETES_MASTER="http://127.0.0.1:8080"
make run

5. Troubleshooting

Schema Validation Errors During CRD Application

When applying a CRD, syntax errors in Kubebuilder tags or type mismatches may trigger the following error:

error: unable to recognize "config/crd/bases/entertainment.cinema.com_movies.yaml": no matches for kind "CustomResourceDefinition" in version "apiextensions.k8s.io/v1"

In this scenario, verify whether the target API server version matches the CRD API specification (v1 or v1beta1). If backward compatibility is required, re-specify crd:crdVersions=v1beta1 in the Controller-tools generation options within the Makefile.

Reconcile Failure Due to Insufficient RBAC Permissions

When running the controller as a Pod in an actual cluster environment, missing RoleBindings for the ServiceAccount will lead to access denial errors such as:

ERROR controllers.Movie unable to fetch Movie {"error": "movies.entertainment.cinema.com is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:cinema-system:cinema-operator\" cannot get resource \"movies\" in API group \"entertainment.cinema.com\""}

This issue originates either from missing RBAC markers (// +kubebuilder:rbac:groups=...) in the Go code or from not applying the generated Role configurations. After updating the markers, re-run make manifests and redeploy the generated ClusterRole/Role manifests.

6. Verification Logs and Execution Protocol

Inspect the logs from CR application and controller startup to verify that the Reconcile process executes correctly.

$ kubectl --server=http://127.0.0.1:8080 get crd
NAME CREATED AT
movies.entertainment.cinema.com 2026-11-11T09:12:44Z

$ kubectl --server=http://127.0.0.1:8080 get movie the-outlaws -o yaml
apiVersion: entertainment.cinema.com/v1
kind: Movie
metadata:
 name: the-outlaws
 namespace: default
spec:
 genre: Action
 isReleased: true
 runningTime: 109
 title: The Outlaws 4

$ make run
/home/user/cinema-operator/bin/controller-gen rbac:roleName=manager-role crd webhook paths="./..." output:crd:artifacts:config=config/crd/bases
go run ./cmd/main.go
2026-11-11T09:15:02.114Z INFO controller-runtime.metrics Metrics server is starting to listen {"addr": ":8080"}
2026-11-11T09:15:02.115Z INFO Starting server {"path": "/metrics", "kind": "metrics", "addr": "[::]:8080"}
2026-11-11T09:15:02.116Z INFO Starting EventSource {"controller": "movie", "controllerGroup": "entertainment.cinema.com", "controllerKind": "Movie", "source": "kind source: *v1.Movie"}
2026-11-11T09:15:02.116Z INFO Starting Controller {"controller": "movie", "controllerGroup": "entertainment.cinema.com", "controllerKind": "Movie"}
2026-11-11T09:15:02.218Z INFO Starting workers {"controller": "movie", "controllerGroup": "entertainment.cinema.com", "controllerKind": "Movie", "worker count": 1}
2026-11-11T09:15:02.219Z INFO Reconciling Movie resource {"controller": "movie", "controllerGroup": "entertainment.cinema.com", "controllerKind": "Movie", "Movie": {"name":"the-outlaws","namespace":"default"}, "namespace": "default", "name": "the-outlaws", "reconcileID": "84e3d179-8ab3-4c91-921c-cb9716ebff12", "Name": "the-outlaws", "Title": "The Outlaws 4", "Genre": "Action", "RunningTime": 109, "IsReleased": true}

7. Architectural Separation Between CRDs and Annotations

When storing custom data in Kubernetes, two primary approaches are considered: using Annotations or introducing a new CRD. The boundary between the two directly impacts system responsibility design.

  • CRD: Used when strict system schema validation is required and a typed API endpoint needs to be established. CRDs are mandatory for constructing the Operator pattern, where other resources (Pods, Jobs, external cloud services, etc.) are actively created, updated, or deleted via the Reconcile loop.
  • Annotation: Used exclusively for attaching incidental metadata, external audit information, or temporary unstructured text. No type validation is performed by the API server.

Operational Notes

When designing custom resources and controllers, the Reconcile logic must be guaranteed to be idempotent. Because the Kubernetes event notification mechanism follows an At-Least-Once delivery model, the logic structure must prevent duplicate resource creation and state inconsistencies even if Reconcile is invoked multiple consecutive times for the same object.

item.title: Kubernetes Application Management Using Helm and Prometheus Monitoring Stack Deployment
item.description:
As the operational scale of a Kubernetes cluster grows, manually deploying and managing static YAML manifests individually leads to configuration bloat and version control confusion. Introducing an abstracted packaging mechanism is essential, particularly when applying identical configurations across multiple environments or managing dependent components collectively. This article explains resource deployment utilizing Helm, the package manager for Kubernetes, alongside procedures for building a visualization and monitoring stack centered on Prometheus and Grafana.

Helm Basic Structure and Operating Principles

Helm achieves dynamic manifest generation by separating the variable configuration file (values.yaml) from a template engine based on Go Template syntax. It manages the application lifecycle using package units called charts.

Standard Chart Directory Structure 

<chart-name>/
├── Chart.yaml # Chart metadata (name, version, API version, etc.)
├── values.yaml # Default parameter values to be injected into templates
├── charts/ # Directory containing dependent subcharts
├── templates/ # Kubernetes manifests written as Go templates
└── .helmignore # File patterns to exclude when packaging

Installing the Helm 3 Binary

Install Helm 3 on the control node to set up the execution environment.

mkdir /root/helm && cd /root/helm
curl -fssL -o get_helm.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3
chmod +x get_helm.sh
./get_helm.sh

After installation completes, verify the version information.

helm version

Example execution log output:

version.BuildInfo{Version:"v3.20.0", GitCommit:"b2e4314fa0f229a1de7b4c981273f61d69ee5a59", GitTreeState:"clean", GoVersion:"go1.25.6"}

Repository Integration and NGINX Chart Parameter Customization

Fetch the chart from an external repository, modify parameters, and deploy it to a specific namespace.

helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami/
helm pull bitnami/nginx
tar zxvf nginx-22.5.5.tgz
mv nginx/ nginx-22.5.5/
cd nginx-22.5.5/

Edit values.yaml to change the replica count from the default value of 1 to 2.

## @param replicaCount Number of NGINX replicas to deploy
##
replicaCount: 2

Create a dedicated namespace and execute the deployment from the chart in the local directory.

kubectl create ns nginx
helm install nginx . --namespace=nginx

Verify the deployment status and rendered manifests.

helm ls -n nginx
helm get manifest nginx -n nginx

Integration of the Observability Stack (Prometheus / Grafana)

For stable Kubernetes cluster operations, metrics collection and visualization at both the node and container layers are essential. This setup integrates the following components:

  • Prometheus: Time-series database (TSDB) and pull-based metrics collection engine
  • Grafana: Dashboard that queries and visualizes data from Prometheus using PromQL
  • Alertmanager: Routes notifications matching alert conditions to external systems
  • kube-state-metrics: Listens to the API server and generates metrics about the state of Kubernetes objects
  • cAdvisor: Embedded in Kubelet to extract per-container CPU and memory resource consumption
  • Node-Exporter: Exposes hardware and kernel metrics at the host OS level

Deploying kube-prometheus-stack

Deploy the entire stack at once using the official chart from Prometheus Community.

helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
helm repo update
helm install monitoring prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --namespace monitoring --create-namespace

Configuring Dashboard Access

Configure port forwarding for the Prometheus UI and Grafana Web UI.

# Prometheus UI port forwarding
kubectl port-forward --address 0.0.0.0 svc/monitoring-kube-prometheus-prometheus 9090:9090 -n monitoring

# Retrieve Grafana admin password
kubectl get secret --namespace monitoring -l app.kubernetes.io/component=admin-secret -o jsonpath="{.items[0].data.admin-password}" | base64 --decode ; echo

# Grafana UI port forwarding
kubectl port-forward --address 0.0.0.0 svc/monitoring-grafana 3000:80 -n monitoring

To apply custom configuration values (e.g., exposure via NodePort), create a custom.yaml for overrides and install with it.

grafana:
 adminPassword: "P@ssw0rd"
 service:
 type: NodePort
 nodePort: 30002

```bash

helm install monitoring . -f custom.yaml -n monitoring

マニフェスト直接定義によるPrometheusデプロイ

Helmを使用できない制限環境向けに、純粋なKubernetesマニフェストを用いてPrometheusを構成する手法を示します。

1. RBAC権限の設定 (prometheus-cluster-role.yaml) 


apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
name: prometheus
namespace: monitoring
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
resources:
- nodes
- nodes/proxy
- services
- endpoints
- pods
verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
- apiGroups:
- extensions
resources:
- ingresses
verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
- nonResourceURLs: ["/metrics"]
verbs: ["get"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
name: prometheus
roleRef:
apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
kind: ClusterRole
name: prometheus
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
name: default
namespace: monitoring

2. ConfigMapによるPrometheus設定 (prometheus-config-map.yaml) 


apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
name: prometheus-server-conf
labels:
name: prometheus-server-conf
namespace: monitoring
data:
prometheus.rules: |-
groups:
- name: container memory alert
rules:
- alert: container memory usage rate is very high( > 55%)
expr: sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod!="", name=""})/ sum (kube_node_status_allocatable_memory_bytes) * 100 > 55
for: 1m
labels:
severity: fatal
annotations:
summary: High Memory Usage
prometheus.yml: |-
global:
scrape_interval: 5s
evaluation_interval: 5s
rule_files:
- /etc/prometheus/prometheus.rules
scrape_configs:
- job_name: 'kubernetes-apiservers'
kubernetes_sd_configs:
- role: endpoints
scheme: https
tls_config:
ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
bearer_token_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
relabel_configs:
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace, __meta_kubernetes_service_name, __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name]
action: keep
regex: default;kubernetes;https
- job_name: 'kubernetes-pods'
kubernetes_sd_configs:
- role: pod
relabel_configs:
- source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape]
action: keep
regex: true

3. DeploymentとDaemonSetの適用 


apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
name: prometheus-deployment
namespace: monitoring
spec:
replicas: 1
selector:
matchLabels:
app: prometheus-server
template:
metadata:
labels:
app: prometheus-server
spec:
containers:
- name: prometheus
image: prom/prometheus:latest
args:
- "--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
- "--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus/"
ports:
- containerPort: 9090
volumeMounts:
- name: prometheus-config-volume
mountPath: /etc/prometheus/
- name: prometheus-storage-volume
mountPath: /prometheus/
volumes:
- name: prometheus-config-volume
configMap:
defaultMode: 420
name: prometheus-server-conf
- name: prometheus-storage-volume
emptyDir: {}

Troubleshooting

1. リポジトリ未登録によるチャート検索エラー

Helmのインストール直後に helm search repo を実行すると以下のエラーが発生します。


Error: no repositories configured

⚠️ 原因: ローカルキャッシュにリモートリポジトリ情報が存在しないためです。 🛠️ 解決策: helm repo add を実行し、対象のリポジトリを追加した後に helm repo update を行ってインデックスを更新します。

2. ポートフォワーディング接続の拒否

kubectl port-forward を実行した際、外部クライアントからアクセスできない現象が発生することがあります。

⚠️ 原因: デフォルトでは 127.0.0.1（ループバックアドレス）にのみバインドされるためです。 🛠️ 解決策: 明示的に –address 0.0.0.0 パラメータを付与して全ネットワークインタフェースからのトラフィックを許可します。

3. PrometheusのAPIスクレイピングにおける403 Forbidden

カスタムマニフェストでPrometheusをデプロイした際、kubernetes-nodes や kubernetes-pods のターゲット取得に失敗するケースがあります。

⚠️ 原因: ServiceAccountに対するRBAC ClusterRoleの権限不足（/metrics エンジンのアクセス権限欠落）です。 🛠️ 解決策: ClusterRoleマニフェストにおいて nonResourceURLs: ["/metrics"] に対する get 権限を明示的に付与してください。

システム検証プロトコル

デプロイ完了後、監視スタックが正常に稼働しているかを端末ログから検証します。


$ kubectl get pods -n monitoring
NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE
alertmanager-monitoring-kube-prometheus-alertmanager-0 2/2 Running 0 10m
monitoring-grafana-7678d7857c-x98kp 1/1 Running 0 10m
monitoring-kube-prometheus-operator-7988fc5dcd-n4z92 1/1 Running 0 10m
monitoring-kube-state-metrics-569d9c7d8b-z2xlj 1/1 Running 0 10m
monitoring-prometheus-node-exporter-4z88k 1/1 Running 0 10m
prometheus-monitoring-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 2/2 Running 0 10m

$ helm ls -n monitoring
NAME NAMESPACE REVISION UPDATED STATUS CHART APP VERSION
monitoring monitoring 1 2026-07-27 10:15:22.123456789 +0900 KST deployed kube-prometheus-stack-58.2.0 v0.72.0</chart-name>
